overview.summary: Robotics engineers design, build and test robots and automated machines, combining mechanical design, electronics and software.
overview.problems: They create machines that help in factories, hospitals, homes, farms and dangerous places.
overview.worksWith: Mechanical, electrical and software engineers, technicians, researchers and customers.
overview.workplaces: Laboratories, factories, research institutes and technology companies, in design offices and workshops.

timeline.title: Team check-in
timeline.description: The engineer reviews progress and problems with the robot project.
timeline.why: Robotics needs mechanical, electrical and software teams to match.

timeline.title: Designing and programming
timeline.description: The engineer designs parts, chooses sensors and motors and writes code to control movement.
timeline.why: Each part must work with the others.

timeline.title: Building and testing
timeline.description: The engineer assembles prototypes and tests how they move and respond.
timeline.why: Testing shows what design on paper cannot.

timeline.title: Debugging
timeline.description: The engineer finds why a robot behaves unexpectedly, which may be a software bug, a loose wire or a faulty sensor.
timeline.why: Problems can hide in software, electronics or mechanics.

timeline.title: Safety checks and documentation
timeline.description: The engineer checks safety measures and records the results.
timeline.why: Moving machines can hurt people if safety is neglected.

timeline.title: Demonstrations and deadlines
timeline.description: Demonstrations for customers or competitions can mean long hours.

responsibilities: Designing and building robots and automated systems
challenges: Problems can come from software, electronics or mechanics, which makes fault finding hard.
Prototypes often fail before they work.
Long projects and deadlines for demonstrations add pressure.
The role needs a wide mix of skills.
Competition for jobs is strong and an engineering degree is often needed.
workEnvironment: Laboratories, workshops and offices, with a mix of design, building and testing. Hours are usually regular, with extra effort before demonstrations. Some roles involve visits to factories or customers.
rewards: Seeing a machine you built move and work
A mix of hardware and software
tradeoffs: Pay and opportunities that vary by country and employer

activity.title: Write robot instructions for a human robot
steps: Place a small object on a table and choose a start spot.
Write step-by-step instructions for a friend, who acts as a robot, to pick it up and place it in a box, using only simple commands such as step forward, turn left and grab.
Test the instructions exactly as written, with no extra help from your friend.
Fix the instructions where the robot got stuck.
Note whether this kind of precise thinking felt interesting.
activity.outcome: You practise breaking tasks into exact steps and debugging, the way robots are programmed.
activity.safety: Do this in a clear space with no sharp or breakable objects, and do not build machines that use mains power or heat.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
